newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Singapore PM says Cambodia poised for ASEAN.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PM says Cambodia poised for ASEAN.

text.p: Cambodia was on track to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in July next year, Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Tuesday.

"I think Cambodia will probably be ahead of Laos and Myanmar (Burma)," Goh, referring to two other countries with ASEAN observer status, said at the end of a two-day visit to Cambodia. "Cambodia will probably be earlier than the others."
Cambodia had made progress towards rehabilition, Goh said. But he added that he still had some lingering concerns over political stability in the country.
"The message the Cambodian government has to put across is that...whatever happens in the upcoming elections, the ruling government will do a lot for foreign investors," he said.

Goh said Cambodia's progress made it ripe for investment, particularly in tourism, light industry and rice production. He added that ASEAN membership would likely spur more investor confidence in the country.
"There is this spirit of resilience here," he said in a speech to a business seminar held by Cambodian co-Premiers Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh. "This country is now reborn."
Singapore is Cambodia's leading trading partner, with more than $350 million in investment in the first eight months of 1996, said Cambodia's Minister of Commerce, Cham Prasidh.
Cambodia, which installed a coalition government in U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, is expected to hold national elections again in 1998.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Goh, who left Cambodia on Tuesday afternoon, signed a bilateral investment agreement, formalized air links between the two countries and opened a $46 million joint venture brewery during his visit.
